title: Cells: the body's building blocks
examples: What is the main job of the nucleus in a cell?
Can you explain the difference between plant and animal cells?
How do cells keep things from getting in?

explain.say: Today we learn about cells, the tiny building blocks of life.
The nucleus is like the cell's control centre, holding the instructions.
The cell membrane surrounds the cell, controlling what goes in and out.
Cells are not all the same; we have different types for different jobs.
Think about a cell membrane acting like a security guard at a gate.
A common mistake is thinking all cells look exactly the same size.

faq.q: What is the main job of the nucleus in a cell?
faq.a: The nucleus holds the cell's genetic material, which contains the instructions for the cell to live and work.
asks: Where are the cell's instructions kept?

faq.q: How does the cell membrane work as a boundary?
faq.a: The cell membrane acts like a selective barrier, deciding which substances can enter or leave the cell.
asks: Does the cell membrane let everything pass?
What controls what enters the cell?

faq.q: Are all body cells the same type?
faq.a: No, the body has many different types of cells, each specialized for a specific job, like muscle or nerve cells.
asks: Do all cells do the same thing?
What makes a skin cell different from a blood cell?

faq.q: Why do we need different cell types?
faq.a: Different jobs require different tools, so specialized cells perform specific tasks to keep the body working correctly.
asks: Why can't one cell do everything?
What is the benefit of having many cell types?

faq.q: What is the difference between the nucleus and the cell membrane?
faq.a: The nucleus is inside and holds the instructions, while the cell membrane is the outer boundary that controls passage.
asks: What is the function of the outer layer?

facts: The nucleus contains the cell's DNA, which carries instructions.
The cell membrane controls the passage of substances into and out of the cell.
Different body parts use different types of cells for their specific functions.
Muscle cells are specialized for movement.

quiz.say: Which part acts as the cell's control centre?
quiz.why: The nucleus is correctly identified as the control centre because it houses the cell's DNA instructions.

wrong.0: This is wrong because DNA is the material inside, not the entire control centre structure.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the cell membrane is the boundary, not the control centre.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance filling the cell.

quiz.say: If a cell needs to send a signal quickly, which type of cell is likely involved?
quiz.why: Nerve cells are specialized for sending electrical signals throughout the body.

wrong.0: This is wrong because muscle cells are specialized for physical movement.
wrong.2: This is wrong because skin cells are mainly for protection and covering.
wrong.3: This is wrong because blood cells are specialized for carrying oxygen.

quiz.say: Which structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
quiz.why: The cell membrane is the correct answer because its job is to act as a gatekeeper for the cell.

wrong.0: This is wrong because DNA is the instruction manual, not the barrier.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the cytoplasm fills the cell and supports the organelles.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the nucleus controls the cell's activities, not its physical boundary.
